item.title: Week Ahead for FX, Bonds: Key Labor Data in Focus Ahead of Fed’s December Rate Decision
item.content:encoded: U.S. labor market data, including the key nonfarm payrolls report, will be in focus in the week starting Nov. 30.

item.title: U.S. Consumer Confidence Came Roaring Back in November, Conference Board Says
item.content:encoded: The research group said its consumer confidence index rose to 103.3 this month from 91.9 in October. Economists polled by The Wall Street Journal had expected a much smaller uptick to 92.2.

item.title: Canada Retail Sales Pull Back After 0.8% Rise in September
item.content:encoded: Canadian retail sales are heading for the sharpest drop in more than a year and a half, a possible sign of cracks in the resilience of household spending and slowing momentum for the economy.

item.title: Consumer Sentiment Climbed in November
item.content:encoded: Consumer sentiment improved in November, according to the University of Michigan’s monthly survey, yet it remains near historically low levels that reflect Americans’ widespread economic frustrations.

item.title: U.K. Consumer Confidence Picks Up Despite Rising Headwinds
item.content:encoded: Consumer sentiment recovered slightly, though inflation concerns and higher interest rates are set to continue weighing on household budgets in the coming months.

item.title: Shoppers’ complaints about food prices could soon grow louder, as surging energy costs and supply-chain delays are elevating costs for producers: “The worst is yet to come”
item.content:encoded: Grocery prices could increase again as surging energy costs and supply-chain delays are lifting costs for producers.

item.title: U.S. Consumer Mood Improved but Remained Gloomy This Month
item.content:encoded: The University of Michigan survey’s preliminary November index reading was 51, up from 48 in the final October reading.

item.title: U.S. prepares to raise tariffs on China and other countries
item.content:encoded: Higher levies to target excess industrial capacity overseas are expected this week.

item.title: China to Suspend Some Critical-Material Export Curbs to U.S. Until January
item.content:encoded: China extended its suspension of export restrictions on some critical materials to the U.S., just days after last week’s Shenzhen summit between President Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping.

item.title: China’s Industrial Profit Surged Despite Headwinds
item.content:encoded: China’s industrial profit surged in October despite mounting domestic headwinds, as robust global demand for its tech products continued to turbocharge exports.

item.title: Germany and France on Diverging Economic Paths, Surveys Show
item.content:encoded: The eurozone’s two largest economies are on diverging paths, with Germany seeing its strongest expansion in more than four years as France struggled to grow.

item.title: A Quarter of Key Goods Vulnerable to Supply Disruptions, Study Finds
item.content:encoded: The disruptions could have damaging consequences for the economies that import these key goods, according to a study by the McKinsey Global Institute.

item.title: U.S. Housing Starts Climb Past Forecasts in October
item.content:encoded: The Commerce Department’s gauge of new residential construction, rose 9.9% in October to 1.309 million, compared with economists expectations of 1.25 million.

item.title: Canada Housing Starts Fall 2.2% in October
item.content:encoded: Housing starts across Canada came in at a seasonally adjusted annualized rate in September of 244,558 units, a 2.2% decline from the month before.

item.title: Bank of Korea Resumes Rate Hikes as AI Boom Fuels Growth

item.title: BOJ’s Tamura Urges Timely Rate Hikes, Bolstering Case for December Move
item.content:encoded: Naoki Tamura said the central bank needs to bring the policy rate to a neutral level soon, as financial conditions remain accommodative.

item.title: Bank of Canada Gov. Macklem Expects Inflation to Remain Persistent
item.content:encoded: Though Canada’s inflation might not accelerate as much as anticipated, survey responses and historical evidence point to more price increases stemming from the Middle East conflict, Macklem said.
